headline: Generative and language-model design extends binders to multi-variant, multi-epitope and motif-level targets
label: Computational Antibody And Binder Design
summary: Preprints this week pair experimental readouts with design across antigen variants, IgE removal, de novo proteins and PDZ peptides, alongside a CDR language-model paper.
synthesis: The common thread is design of binders optimized for objectives beyond a single-target affinity score. An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for affinity and specificity. Germinal Multi jointly optimizes one paratope against multiple antigen variants, with designs binding EGFR variants and neutralizing SARS-CoV-2. Claude-enabled agentic design yields biparatopic IgE disruptors, three of which outperform omalizumab at removing bound IgE. Pallatom2 models sequence, backbone, side chains and target contacts jointly at the atom level, and a PDZ-binding peptide method designs motifs through directions in a shared latent space learned from affinity prediction. What is new is the breadth of design formats and of functional endpoints; the items differ in modality and evidence, and the summaries do not allow cross-method comparison of performance.
